Threat: Phishing email captures a staff password
Vulnerability: MFA is optional; no phishing training since onboarding
Consequence: Attacker reads mail and shared drives, resets passwords for other tools, sends invoices as the company
Planned controls: Enforce MFA for all accounts; quarterly phishing simulation; short awareness training twice a year

Threat: Bucket or object made public by mistake
Vulnerability: Buckets created by hand; no automated configuration check
Consequence: Customer rosters and staff personal data exposed on the internet; GDPR breach notification within 72 hours
Existing controls: Account-level Block Public Access on production account only
Planned controls: Block Public Access on every account; infrastructure as code with policy scan in CI; weekly configuration report

Threat: Ransomware delivered by attachment or download
Vulnerability: Endpoint protection not centrally managed; local admin rights on laptops
Consequence: Files encrypted, 2-5 days of lost work, possible data theft and extortion
Existing controls: Built-in OS antivirus, shared drive version history
Planned controls: Managed EDR on all laptops; remove local admin; cyber insurance policy to cover response cost

Threat: Former employee or contractor still has access
Vulnerability: Leaver process is a manual checklist; no central identity provider
Consequence: Unauthorised access to customer data or source code after the person has left
Existing controls: HR emails IT on the last working day
Planned controls: Single sign-on for all core tools; leaver checklist owned by People team with same-day deadline; quarterly access review

Threat: Known vulnerability in a library or container image is exploited
Vulnerability: No patch deadline; dependency updates done when someone remembers
Consequence: Remote compromise of the application and access to the customer database
Planned controls: Patch deadlines by severity (critical 7 days, high 30 days); dependency and image scan in CI that blocks release; annual penetration test

Vulnerability: Database runs in one availability zone; recovery never tested
Consequence: Service down for all customers for hours; SLA credits and churn
Planned controls: Multi-AZ database; documented recovery procedure with RTO 4h / RPO 1h; recovery test twice a year

Vulnerability: No supplier security review; contracts not checked for security or breach clauses
Consequence: Customer personal data exposed through a third party; the company is still accountable as processor
Existing controls: Data processing agreements signed with the two largest suppliers
Planned controls: Supplier register with risk tiering; security questionnaire and DPA for every sub-processor; annual review of critical suppliers

Threat: Backup is corrupt, incomplete or cannot be restored
Vulnerability: Restore has never been tested; backups kept in the same account as production
Consequence: Permanent loss of customer data after an incident
Planned controls: Quarterly restore test with written result; copy of backups in a separate account; retention raised to 35 days

Threat: Engineer misuses or exports customer data
Vulnerability: All eight engineers have standing read/write access to production
Consequence: Confidentiality breach by an insider; hard to detect or prove
Planned controls: Remove standing access; time-limited access with approval and ticket reference; query logging on production

Threat: Data subject request or breach handled late or incorrectly
Vulnerability: No record of processing activities; no written DSAR or breach procedure
Consequence: Complaint to the Data Protection Commission, enforcement action, loss of customer trust
Planned controls: Record of processing activities; DSAR and breach notification procedures with named owner; annual privacy training

Threat: Laptop lost or stolen while travelling or working remotely
Vulnerability: Disk encryption not verified on every device; no remote wipe
Consequence: Local copies of customer exports and saved sessions exposed
Planned controls: Device management tool enforcing disk encryption and remote wipe; device inventory

Threat: API key or database password committed to a repository
Vulnerability: No secret scanning; secrets shared in chat and .env files
Consequence: Attacker with repository access (or a leaked clone) reaches production systems directly
Planned controls: Secret scanning with push protection; secrets manager for all credentials; rotate every key found in history

Threat: Unreviewed or untested change released to production
Vulnerability: Branch protection off; any engineer can deploy from a laptop
Consequence: Outage or security defect introduced; no record of who changed what
Planned controls: Branch protection with mandatory review; deploys only through the pipeline; change log kept automatically

Threat: Attack is not noticed for weeks
Vulnerability: Logs kept on each system for 7 days; nobody reviews them; no alerts
Consequence: Longer attacker dwell time, larger breach, and no evidence to investigate or to report accurately
Planned controls: Central log store with 12-month retention; alerts for admin logins, failed logins and privilege changes; incident response plan with on-call owner

Threat: The one DevOps engineer leaves or is unavailable
Vulnerability: Infrastructure knowledge and root credentials held by one person; nothing written down
Consequence: Slow or failed recovery during an incident; delayed releases
Planned controls: Runbooks for deploy, restore and incident response; second trained administrator; break-glass credentials in a sealed vault

Threat: Real customer data exposed through weaker test systems
Vulnerability: Production database copied to staging for debugging
Consequence: Personal data held where access control and logging are weaker; breach of data minimisation
Planned controls: Stop copying production data; generate synthetic or masked data sets for testing

Threat: Visitor enters the office area and takes a device or reads a screen
Vulnerability: Building reception is shared; no visitor log for the company's floor
Consequence: Loss of one device or limited disclosure of on-screen information
Existing controls: Badge access to the floor, clear desk expected, laptops taken home
Planned controls: None planned. Accepted by the CEO; review at next assessment or if the office changes
